title: Required flags are unmarked in the usage line and inexpressible in the manifest (lore impact --direction and four more)
description:
`lore impact` requires `--direction`, and its usage line does not say so. Reported by downstream
validation on host mbpm2 against the published 0.6.2 (2026-09-14), alongside an otherwise PASSING
run; explicitly not a regression and not urgent.

MEASURED ON dev AT 661529cf, not inferred. `lore help impact` prints:

    Usage:
      lore impact <id>

    Flags:
      --kind <value>        Typed root: concept or task
      --direction <value>   Traversal direction: outbound, inbound, or either
      --edge <value>        Allow one authored edge kind (repeatable)
      ...

Every flag renders in one undifferentiated list, so `--direction` looks exactly as optional as
`--limit`. It is not: `src/commands/traversal.ts:29` resolves it through `requiredChoice`, which
throws a usage error when it is absent.

THE REPORTER FOUND ONE INSTANCE; THERE ARE FIVE, ACROSS TWO COMMANDS. `requiredChoice` is called for
`impact`'s `--kind` and `--direction`, and for `path`'s `--from-kind`, `--to-kind` and `--direction`
(`src/commands/traversal.ts:29,45`). All five are mandatory and none is marked. Fixing only the one
that was reported would leave four identical defects behind.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS IN THE CONTRACT, NOT THE RENDERER. `ManifestFlag` (`src/core/manifest.ts:52`) has
`name`, `alias`, `takesValue`, `repeatable`, `summary` and `kind` -- and no way whatsoever to express
that a flag is required. So the help renderer is not omitting information it has; it has none to
omit, and neither does anyone reading `lore manifest --json`.

THAT SECOND CONSEQUENCE IS THE SERIOUS ONE AND IS WHY THIS IS WORTH MORE THAN A HELP-TEXT TWEAK. The
manifest is a MACHINE CONTRACT -- it exists so an agent can enumerate what the CLI accepts without
reading its source. An agent doing that today is told `--direction` is an ordinary optional flag,
constructs `lore impact <id> --kind task`, and gets exit 2. The CLI is describing a command that
does not exist. The same class of defect is what LCLI-366 fixed for `--version` (a flag that
terminates with its own envelope, previously undeclared): the manifest must be able to say the
thing, not just the help text.

SHAPE OF A FIX, not prescribed: add an optional `required?: boolean` to `ManifestFlag` -- additive,
so a consumer that does not know the field is unaffected, which is the same property that made the
LCLI-366 `kind` field safe -- render it in the usage line and/or the flag list, and set it on the
five flags above.

AUDIT THE WHOLE SURFACE, NOT THE FIVE. Other commands enforce requirements through ad-hoc
`throw usage(...)` calls rather than `requiredChoice`, some of them CONDITIONAL rather than absolute:
`--force requires --out` (`src/commands/agent.ts:428`), `--repository requires --workspace`
(`src/commands/args.ts:181`), `--from and --to must be supplied together` and
`--workspace requires retained snapshot selectors` (`src/commands/explorer.ts:169,172`). A plain
boolean cannot express those. Decide deliberately whether they are in scope, and if they are not,
say so rather than leaving the reader to wonder why some mandatory flags are marked and others are
not.

Small, real, and the reporter's description was enough to act on.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `lore help impact` distinguishes its REQUIRED flags (`--kind`, `--direction`) from its optional ones, and `lore help path` does the same for `--from-kind`, `--to-kind` and `--direction` -- all five, not only the one that was reported.

`lore manifest --json` expresses requiredness machine-readably, so an agent enumerating the contract can tell a mandatory flag from an optional one. The field is ADDITIVE, so a consumer that does not know it is unaffected -- the same property that made the LCLI-366 `kind` field safe.

A test ties the manifest's required markers to the actual parser, so a flag that becomes required, or stops being, cannot silently drift from what the manifest claims. Verified mutation-sensitive: flip one marker and the test must fail.

Every command is audited for the same defect, not only the two the reporter's tooling reached. Flags enforced by ad-hoc `throw usage(...)` rather than `requiredChoice` -- `--force requires --out`, `--repository requires --workspace`, `--from`/`--to` together, `--workspace requires retained snapshot selectors` -- are either covered or EXPLICITLY ruled out of scope with a reason, so the next reader is not left wondering why some mandatory flags are marked and others are not.
If the manifest carries a schema version that this change affects, it is bumped and its contract test updated; if it does not, that is stated rather than left implicit.
`bun run lint`, `typecheck` and the test suite pass, and `lore check` exits 0.
